narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Plutarch recounts a road encounter at Epidaurus: Periphetes carries a club and tries to stop Theseus from continuing.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “himself of all those that should offer any. And first of all, in a set combat, he slew Periphetes, in the neighborhood of Epidaurus, who used a club for his arms, and from thence had the name of Corynetes, or the club-bearer; who seized upon him, and forbade him to go forward in his journey. Being pleased”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Plutarch says Theseus defeats Periphetes and takes the club as his own weapon; this is one episode in a later biography.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: This passage supports a claim about Plutarch's account, not eyewitness documentation of a historical journey.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: A founder myth turns heroic violence into a claim about safety and shared identity.

quiz.prompt: What weapon is associated with Periphetes in Plutarch's account?
quiz.explanation: Plutarch calls Periphetes the club-bearer because he uses a club.

quiz.prompt: What does Theseus do with Periphetes' club?

choices.text: He buries it under the olive bed
He takes it and carries it as his own weapon
He gives it to the Minotaur

quiz.explanation: Plutarch says Theseus takes the club and afterward carries it as his own weapon.
